findings.title: Modern protection is advertised
findings.explanation: WPA2 or WPA3 protects the wireless link when correctly negotiated. It does not establish who operates the network.

findings.title: An open connection is advertised
findings.explanation: The open connection does not encrypt the Wi-Fi link. HTTPS still protects correctly secured website content. A sign-in page does not itself add Wi-Fi encryption.

findings.title: Same name, different protection
findings.explanation: Access points with this name advertise different settings. Reconfiguration, unrelated operators, or copying the name can explain it. Ask the venue what to expect; this scan cannot identify the cause.

findings.title: Modern protection is advertised
findings.explanation: WPA2 or WPA3 protects the wireless link when correctly negotiated. It does not establish who operates the network.

findings.title: Several access points share this name
findings.explanation: This is normal for larger venues and mesh networks. A shared name does not prove shared ownership, and unavailable settings remain unknown.

findings.title: Modern protection is advertised
findings.explanation: WPA2 or WPA3 protects the wireless link when correctly negotiated. It does not establish who operates the network.

findings.title: Some protection details are unavailable
findings.explanation: The phone did not provide security settings this version can interpret. Missing information does not mean an attack.

findings.title: Older protection needs attention
findings.explanation: WEP and original WPA are outdated. Prefer another network you can use, or your own hotspot. This setting does not establish malicious intent.

reasons: You confirmed permission and access to this network.
WPA2 advertised; strong signal in this observation.
Compared advertised protection, then broad signal strength. Neither establishes operator trust or internet speed.
recommendation.explanation: An option to consider among the Wi-Fi you said you can use. Confirm the name and sign-in instructions with staff.

limitations: Fictional demonstration observations only. This report does not describe nearby Wi-Fi or a live scan.
This shared report is a snapshot. Conditions and access permissions may have changed since export.
A scan cannot confirm who runs a network. Names and advertised settings can be copied.
Signal strength does not measure internet speed, congestion, or reliability.
Ordinary phone scans cannot observe deauthentication traffic or verify a sign-in page.
The phone may return cached or incomplete observations. Recommendations require a successful scan and observations no older than 30 seconds.
WiFi Scout never joins automatically. Confirm the network with the venue, then use Android Wi-Fi settings.
